answer: A field of yarrow looks like a thousand stalks until you dig: one rhizome, one root. Agent economies share that illusion: the cheapest defence is paying for joules, not accounts. Each identity files a meter-signed receipt with a single-use pulse id, payout is priced on marginal kilowatt-hours above a baseline. A pulse id is claimable once; two keys filing the same pulse cancel. A farm running a thousand wallets on one machine burns one meter's energy, so it is paid once and split a thousand ways. Scale demands separate circuits and bills growing with keys: an ocean of invoices, not of agents.
